title: The Effect of Individual Online Reviews on Purchase Likelihood
eligible_reason: Not a staggered DiD. Session-level regressions of purchase on the ratings of reviews in each page position with product and week fixed effects and time-varying controls (average rating, number of reviews, mobile, weekend), plus a regression-discontinuity-in-time design around the arrival of a new 5-star review in position one (product FE only, no calendar-time FE, narrow windows, time-varying controls). Not a binary policy adopted at unit-specific dates in a TWFE panel.
design_notes: DO_File_Tables_MS_Simulated.do: reg buy pos1_2-pos5_5 wordsp1-5 avgrating other4avg numreviews mobile weekend i.pid i.week, vce(cluster pid) (Tables 2, 4-6, 8, 10, 12-13). DO_File_Tables_RD_Simulated.do: reg buy after (or befrat1-4) avgrating avgrat25 numreviews words1-5 mobile weekend i.productid within 14-day windows around each new review (Tables 7-11). The RD compares sessions just before and after each review event, one window per event, with no comparison units at the same calendar time.
data_files_note: Readme.txt: under NDA 'the data made available masks the original data by adding some random noise to a few variables'; outputs do not exactly match the paper.
data_provenance_note: Original sessions with random noise added to some variables (files labeled 'Simulated').
